messages:
maria_dev: Heads up — saw a cluster autoscaler loop in eu-west yesterday where GPU nodegroups were scaling up fine but a bunch of nodes stayed around for hours. Looks tied to network probe flaps + PDBs. Anyone seen similar?

sam_platform: Yep saw that around 03:40 UTC. Nodes went NotReady for a few mins due to a managed VPC route-update, CA didn't drain because of PDBs and then unready timers kept them from being removed.

ian_infra: Logs I pulled: autoscaler reported Unremovable: 8 nodes, reason: "pdb violation" and "pod not terminating (kubelet not responding)". Also a bunch of GPU pods with long InitContainers (nvdriver startup).

jenna_sre: Quick data point: GPU instances have ~4–6m extra boot time (drivers + device plugin). With network flaps that got extended. I think our --max-node-provision-time is 15m, but --scale-down-unready-time is 5m which conflicts.

autoscaler-bot: [metric] CA:scale-up-events: +12 (03:35-03:50), scale-down-failed: 9, avg.scale-down-delay-after-add: 6m.

ops-oncall: Command I ran: `kubectl get pods -A -o wide | egrep "Evicted|ContainerCreating|NodeNotReady"` — showed several pods stuck in ContainerCreating waiting for attach/detach and kubelet registration.

maria_dev: Proposed mitigations I'm tossing around: bump --scale-down-unready-time for GPU nodegroups to 20m; increase --scale-down-delay-after-add to 10m; change expander to least-waste for GPU pools so CA favors packing instead of spreading. Thoughts?

sam_platform: +1 on per-nodegroup tuning. We should not globally increase unready time (that would keep other noisy nodes around). Use tags/labels to detect gpu nodegroups and run CA with nodeGroup autoDiscovery + separate flags? CA doesn't support per-group flags though.

ian_infra: Workaround: split GPU pools into a dedicated ASG/nodegroup and run a separate CA instance for GPU pools with different flags (we do this for spot vs reserved currently). That gives us per-pool flags: e.g., `--scale-down-unready-time=20m --max-node-provision-time=30m --expander=least-waste`.

jenna_sre: Also consider `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` for GPU groups lower (0.4 -> 0.25) so CA is more willing to remove underutilized GPU nodes once PDBs clear. But be careful — lower threshold can cause churn if scheduling bursts are common.

maria_dev: Another behavioral fix: add a pre-drain check for network readiness (or a drain hook that waits for kubelet to respond before evict). We could add a kubelet readiness probe check in our drain script: if NodeCondition NetworkUnavailable or NodeReady==False for <x> then postpone drain.

ops-oncall: PV attach/detach is also a blocker — those mounts delay evictions and CA logs show "volumeMount in use". We should increase CSI attach timeout and check cloud provider detach lulls during AZ rebalancing.

ian_infra: Notes on flags we experimented with in a canary GPU CA: 
```
--expander=least-waste
--max-node-provision-time=30m
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
--ignore-daemonsets-utilization=true
```
That reduced stuck nodes by ~70% during a simulated network patch.

sam_platform: Ops checklist if we roll this: 1) spin separate CA for gpu nodegroups; 2) add a label selector in CA discovery e.g. `--nodes=pool=gpu-*`; 3) update runbook for oncall to check PDBs and PVs before force-drain; 4) monitor scale-down-failed metric and set alert at >3/min for 30m.

maria_dev: Agreed. I'll prototype separate CA for gpu-eu-west and gpu-us and run it during a low-traffic window. I'll also add a short script to detect transient network flaps and annotate nodes with `autoscaler/provision-wait` to keep CA from touching them.

jenna_sre: One more: consider increasing `--max-empty-bulk-delete` for GPU pool so CA can remove multiple idle nodes once PDBs are resolved. But test first.

ops-oncall: Thanks — will watch the canary and flag any odd quota/cost changes. :eyes:

maria_dev: I'll open a PR with the infra changes + runbook edits and link it here when ready. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
